definition: Clinical Modern Standard Arabic phrase for bisexual, literally 'dual of sex/gender'; used in formal health and human-rights discourse about sexual orientation.
notes: Calque construction; competes with مزدوج الميل الجنسي in formal academic writing; recognition limited to educated and LGBTQ+-informed speakers.

definition: Clinical MSA phrase for heterosexual, literally 'contrary/different of sex'; used mainly in LGBTQ+ and medical contexts where heterosexuality must be explicitly named rather than assumed as default.
notes: Arabic discourse rarely needs to name heterosexuality explicitly because it is the unmarked norm; this clinical phrase appears almost exclusively in texts that must enumerate orientation categories.

definition: Clinical MSA phrase for asexual, literally 'non-sexual'; describes a person who experiences little or no sexual attraction to others.
notes: Asexuality as a named identity category is poorly represented in Arabic-language discourse; recognition essentially limited to highly educated LGBTQ+-informed speakers; competes with the calque لاجنسي.

definition: Clinical MSA calque of 'transgender', literally 'crossing/transcending sex-gender'; the preferred neutral identity term in Arabic LGBTQ+ advocacy and human-rights writing.
notes: Foregrounds identity and gender crossing rather than medical transition; distinguishable from متحول جنسياً which emphasizes bodily change; preferred by activists but uncommon in mainstream Arabic media.

definition: Classical Arabic and Islamic jurisprudence term for a person with ambiguous or mixed sex characteristics; codified in fiqh to govern inheritance, dress, and ritual obligations; in modern colloquial use can be repurposed as a slur for effeminate men.
notes: The classical fiqh category distinguishes khunthā wāḍiḥ (unambiguous hermaphrodite) from khunthā mushkil (ambiguous); the term predates the modern intersex concept and carries no malice in religious-legal discourse but has acquired a derogatory colloquial register when applied to men without ambiguous biology.

definition: Formal MSA phrase for bisexual, literally 'dual/double of sexual inclination'; the more verbose academic variant used in psychology, sexology, and public-health writing.
notes: More technically precise than ثنائي الجنسية by naming 'inclination' (mayl) rather than 'sex/gender' as the doubled element; found primarily in academic texts and formal health communications; low recognition outside specialist contexts.

definition: MSA clinical phrase for transsexual or transgender, literally 'sexually/gender-transformed'; emphasizes bodily or social transition and is the most common term in Arabic news coverage and medical discourse about trans people.
notes: More widely used than عابر الجنس in mainstream Arabic media; carries stronger connotation of medical transition (surgery, hormones) than identity alone; the adverb جنسياً can imply sexual deviance to conservative readers, giving the phrase a slightly loaded quality absent from the activist-preferred عابر الجنس.

definition: Clinical MSA noun phrase for 'sexual attraction' as an abstract orientation-framework concept; used to name the phenomenon of being drawn to others sexually, independent of direction, in academic and LGBTQ+-discourse contexts.
notes: Proposed slug: sexual_attraction_concept. The registry has no generic 'sexual attraction as orientation concept' entry distinct from states of arousal or specific same-sex attraction categories; this term functions as the Arabic equivalent of 'sexual attraction' when used abstractly in orientation definitions such as 'same-sex attraction' (الانجذاب الجنسي المثلي).

definition: Arabic phonetic transliteration of the English 'pansexual'; used exclusively in LGBTQ+-informed Arabic social-media and activist contexts to describe attraction regardless of gender.
notes: Very recent borrowing with no established MSA calque alternative; virtually absent outside online Arabic LGBTQ+ communities; low recognition even among educated speakers unfamiliar with queer-identity discourse.

definition: Arabic calque of 'asexual' formed with the negative prefix لā; describes a person experiencing little or no sexual attraction; used primarily in online Arabic LGBTQ+ spaces.
notes: The morphological structure (لا + جنسي) mirrors the English 'a-' + 'sexual' prefix logic, making it community-coined rather than formally adopted; competes with غير جنسي in the same semantic space; recognition negligible outside identity-aware speakers.

definition: The primary Islamic condemnatory term for a gay man or sodomite, derived from the Prophet Lūṭ (Lot) whose people in Sodom practiced anal intercourse between men; carries severe religious-moral condemnation across all Arabic-speaking societies.
notes: Cognate with the act-noun liwāṭ (اللواط, sodomy); one of the oldest and most universally recognized Arabic terms for homosexuality; simultaneously a formal religious-legal category and a devastating street-level slur; deeply embedded in Islamic jurisprudence (the act is a ḥadd offense under some schools).

definition: Derogatory MSA phrase for a homosexual person, literally 'sexually abnormal/deviant'; used in conservative religious discourse and mainstream Arabic media to pathologize homosexuality as a biological or moral aberration.
notes: شاذ (shādhdh) means irregular, exceptional, anomalous; applied to sexuality it frames same-sex attraction as a deviation from natural and divine order; widely used in Arabic-language religious fatwas, state media, and conservative commentary; its register is semi-formal rather than street-slang, lending it the air of authoritative condemnation.

definition: Classical Arabic term for a man who imitates women in appearance, speech, and mannerism; explicitly cursed in hadith literature; used in both classical Islamic texts and contemporary discourse as a slur for effeminate gay men.
notes: The Prophet's curse of al-mutakhannithīn (men who imitate women) and al-mutarajjilāt (women who imitate men) is widely cited in Islamic literature; the Form V verb form takhannatha implies habitual self-directed feminization; the term predates modern homosexual identity categories but is routinely applied to gay men.

definition: Extremely vulgar Egyptian colloquial slur for an effeminate or passive gay man; one of the most offensive Arabic terms for a male who adopts the feminized or receptive role; widely exported via Egyptian cinema and television.
notes: Egyptian dialectal in origin but broadly understood across the Arab world due to Egypt's cultural dominance in film and media; used both as a specific homosexuality slur and as a general-purpose insult disconnected from sexual context, similarly to how 'faggot' functions in colloquial English; considered maximally offensive in formal contexts.

definition: Classical and medieval Arabic term for a man who habitually submits to anal penetration; attested in pre-modern poetry and medical literature as a marker of sexual passivity and extreme social dishonor.
notes: Has attestation in classical Arabic erotic poetry (adab al-jins), medieval medical texts, and adab literature; specifically marks the receptive-passive sexual role as a fixed character type rather than homosexuality in the modern identity sense; recognized by educated speakers but less common in everyday colloquial use than منيوك or خَوَل.

definition: Extremely vulgar colloquial Arabic slur for a man who receives anal penetration; passive participial form of nayk (to fuck), marking the recipient of intercourse; among the most offensive Arabic insults for a passive or gay male.
notes: Derived from نيك (nayk), widely considered the most obscene Arabic verb for sexual intercourse; the passive-participial form (mafʿūl pattern) grammatically positions the target as the acted-upon party; also deployed as a general-purpose insult analogous to 'fucker' but with explicit passivity connotation.

definition: Vulgar colloquial slur for a man who is anally penetrated, derived from qāʿ/qaʿr meaning the bottom or depth of a vessel; marks the receptive sexual role as social-shame category and general insult.
notes: قعر (qaʿr) means the bottom, floor, or pit of a container; applying it to a person implies he is the lowest point, the receptive base; common in Levantine and Gulf colloquial Arabic; shares semantic territory with منيوك but the root imagery emphasizes being at the 'bottom' rather than the act of being penetrated.

definition: Vulgar colloquial Arabic slur for a passive homosexual, derived from daʿaka meaning to rub, grind, or crush; implies the person is physically ground down or worked over in the receptive sexual role.
notes: دعك (daʿk) denotes vigorous rubbing or grinding friction; the passive-participle formation designates the recipient of this action; somewhat regionally variable in distribution compared to منيوك; found across Levantine and North African colloquial Arabic; less widely recognized than the other passive-role slurs in this set.

definition: Colloquial Arabic slur that calls an effeminate or passive gay man a 'bride' or 'daughter-in-law', imposing the feminine-marital role on the target to mark sexual and social shame.
notes: كنّة (kanna) literally means daughter-in-law or bride in various regional dialects; applied to a man it lexically forces him into the feminine-receptive marital role; the insult's force derives from the Arab honor-shame system in which a man occupying a woman's role is profoundly dishonored; regional distribution variable.

definition: Colloquial Arabic slur for an effeminate or nagging gay man, derived from zanna meaning to buzz, drone, or whine; evokes a stereotyped image of an effeminate man who chatters or complains in a high-pitched, womanish manner.
notes: زنّ (zann) denotes the continuous buzzing of an insect or the persistent nagging whine of a person; the intensive form زنّانة amplifies both effeminacy and irritating persistence; particularly common in Egyptian and Levantine colloquial Arabic; the onomatopoeic root adds a quality of contemptuous mockery absent from purely anatomical slurs.

definition: Literally 'feminized' or 'made feminine'; the standard Arabic grammatical term for the feminine gender, repurposed as a mild-to-moderate personal insult for an effeminate man when applied to a person rather than a noun.
notes: Sharply dual-register: in grammatical contexts (الاسم المؤنث, feminine noun) it is entirely neutral and high-frequency; applied to a man as a character descriptor it becomes a derogatory label of effeminacy; crude score reflects the derogatory personal-insult usage; the low crude relative to other slurs in this set reflects the word's overwhelming association with grammar rather than sexuality.

definition: Figurative insult meaning 'spiritually or soulfully castrated'; applies the image of physical castration to a man's inner character to condemn total emasculation of will, courage, and masculine agency.
notes: مخصي = castrated (from khaṣā, to castrate); بالروح = in/of the soul/spirit; weaponizes the extreme dishonor of physical castration and displaces it onto character rather than anatomy; no direct English idiom equivalent; the compound is creative colloquial Arabic rather than a fixed lexical item.

definition: Classical and semi-formal Arabic term for a man who voluntarily adopts feminine characteristics or demeanor; from the Form X verb istaʾnatha, 'to make oneself feminine'; implies deliberate gender-norm transgression.
notes: Form X (istaFʿaLa) morphology encodes deliberate self-directed action, distinguishing it from مؤنث (passively feminized) and متخنث (habitually imitating women): the target is actively choosing femininity; attested in classical texts and survives in formal written Arabic; more literary in register than متخنث.

definition: Extreme Arabic insult branding a man as 'permissible/lawful of the anus'; inverts Islamic halal/haram legal language to declare that his rectum is sexually available to anyone, combining maximal sexual violation with religious desecration.
english_term: one whose ass is open to all (extreme gay slur)
notes: حلال = religiously permissible (halal); الدبر = the back/anus (the classical anatomical term, used in Quranic commentary on the prohibition of anal intercourse); the phrase is specifically Arabic-Islamic in construction, weaponizing the central halal/haram binary as a sexual insult; no English idiom captures the simultaneous attack on sexual honor and religious standing.

definition: Literally 'son of a whore/slut'; شرموطة is one of the most vulgar Arabic terms for a sexually promiscuous woman, so the compound attacks the target's honor through his mother's sexual reputation — the most powerful shaming vector in Arab honor culture.
notes: شرموطة (sharmūṭa) is itself one of the most sexually explicit and offensive Arabic terms for a woman, making this compound substantially more vulgar than its English functional equivalent 'son of a bitch'; strikes at sharaf (honor) via maternal sexual shame, which carries far greater cultural weight in Arab honor-shame systems than in contemporary Western contexts; universal recognition across all Arabic dialects.
